# Question and sampling design

How did cereal rye biomass immediately before termination differ among the three Mowtivation site-years? Rye was sampled within four blocks per site-year before tillage and again, on a later date, before roller-crimping. These are **different sampling occasions**, not a randomized comparison of termination methods. Analyze site-year differences **separately** for each occasion. Results describe the three observed site-years; they cannot isolate effects of rye variety, weather, or termination date.

# Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(emmeans)
library(WrensBookshelf)

theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 16))

out_dir <- here("output", "tables", "pretermination_rye_biomass")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

site_levels <- c("V_2023", "O2E_2024", "O2W_2024")
event_levels <- c("pre-tillage", "pre-rolling")
```

# Import, convert, and validate

The raw file contains quadrat dry biomass in grams and sampled area in square meters. Conversion: `kg/ha = g / m2 * 10` (equivalent to `g * 20` for a 0.5-m2 quadrat).

```{r import-validate}
raw <- readr::read_csv(here("data", "raw", "pretermination_rye_biomass.csv"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
required <- c("site_year", "block", "sampling_date", "event",
              "cereal_rye_variety", "sampling_area_m2", "cereal_rye_biomass_g")
missing_columns <- setdiff(required, names(raw))
if (length(missing_columns)) stop("Missing columns: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))

rye <- raw |>
  mutate(
    site_year = factor(as.character(site_year), levels = site_levels),
    block = factor(block),
    event = factor(trimws(as.character(event)), levels = event_levels),
    sampling_date = as.Date(sampling_date),
    biomass_kg_ha = cereal_rye_biomass_g / sampling_area_m2 * 10
  ) |>
  arrange(site_year, event, block)

stopifnot(
  nrow(rye) == 24L,
  !anyNA(rye[, c("site_year", "block", "event", "sampling_date",
                  "cereal_rye_variety", "sampling_area_m2",
                  "cereal_rye_biomass_g", "biomass_kg_ha")]),
  all(rye$sampling_area_m2 == 0.5),
  all(rye$biomass_kg_ha > 0),
  all(as.vector(table(rye$site_year, rye$event)) == 4L),
  all(as.vector(table(rye$site_year, rye$event, rye$block)) == 1L)
)

readr::write_csv(rye, file.path(out_dir, "block_level_biomass_kg_ha.csv"))
knitr::kable(rye |> count(site_year, event), caption = "Validated quadrat observations")
```

# Descriptive summaries

All means, SDs, and SEs are calculated from **four observed block values** per site-year and sampling event. These SEs are descriptive, not model-based.

```{r summaries}
summary_long <- rye |>
  group_by(site_year, event) |>
  summarise(
    sampling_date = first(sampling_date),
    cereal_rye_variety = first(cereal_rye_variety),
    n_blocks = n(),
    mean_kg_ha = mean(biomass_kg_ha),
    sd_kg_ha = sd(biomass_kg_ha),
    se_kg_ha = sd_kg_ha / sqrt(n_blocks),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

group_checks <- rye |>
  group_by(site_year, event) |>
  summarise(n_dates = n_distinct(sampling_date),
            n_varieties = n_distinct(cereal_rye_variety), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(group_checks$n_dates == 1L),
          all(group_checks$n_varieties == 1L))

summary_wide <- summary_long |>
  mutate(
    sampling_event = recode(as.character(event),
                            `pre-tillage` = "before_tillage",
                            `pre-rolling` = "before_rolling")
  ) |>
  select(site_year, cereal_rye_variety, sampling_event,
         sampling_date, n_blocks, mean_kg_ha, sd_kg_ha, se_kg_ha) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sampling_event,
    values_from = c(sampling_date, n_blocks, mean_kg_ha, sd_kg_ha, se_kg_ha),
    names_glue = "{sampling_event}_{.value}"
  )

readr::write_csv(summary_long, file.path(out_dir, "rye_biomass_summary_long.csv"))
readr::write_csv(summary_wide, file.path(out_dir, "rye_biomass_site_year_table.csv"))
knitr::kable(summary_long |> mutate(across(ends_with("kg_ha"), ~ round(.x, 1))),
             caption = "Observed pre-termination rye biomass (kg/ha)")
knitr::kable(summary_wide |> mutate(across(ends_with("kg_ha"), ~ round(.x, 1))),
             caption = "Wide site-year summary for manuscript table")
```

# Site-year comparisons

Fit separate one-way linear models for the two events. Block is the observational replicate within each site-year (four blocks per site-year). Since each block contributes only one observation *within an event*, adding a block random intercept to these separate models would be unidentifiable from residual variance. We do not interpret differences between event dates as termination effects.

```{r site-year-models}
fit_event <- function(event_name) {
  dat <- rye |> filter(event == event_name) |> droplevels()
  model <- lm(biomass_kg_ha ~ site_year, data = dat)
  test <- anova(model) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("effect") |>
    filter(effect == "site_year") |>
    transmute(event = event_name, effect, df = Df,
              F_value = `F value`, p_value = `Pr(>F)`)
  means <- as.data.frame(confint(emmeans(model, ~ site_year))) |>
    mutate(event = event_name, .before = 1)
  list(model = model, test = test, means = means)
}

models <- setNames(lapply(event_levels, fit_event), event_levels)
anova_results <- bind_rows(lapply(models, `[[`, "test"))
model_means <- bind_rows(lapply(models, `[[`, "means"))

knitr::kable(anova_results, digits = 4,
             caption = "Separate site-year ANOVAs by sampling event")
readr::write_csv(anova_results, file.path(out_dir, "site_year_anova.csv"))
readr::write_csv(model_means, file.path(out_dir, "site_year_model_means.csv"))
```

# Residual checks

With just four blocks per site-year, assess unusually influential observations or marked changes in spread cautiously. The standard linear-model assumptions apply to the **within-event** site-year tests.

```{r diagnostics}
diag_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, function(obj, event_name) {
  tibble(
    event = event_name,
    residual_sd = sigma(obj$model),
    max_abs_standardized_residual = max(abs(rstandard(obj$model))),
    shapiro_p = shapiro.test(resid(obj$model))$p.value
  )
})
knitr::kable(diag_summary, digits = 3,
             caption = "Simple residual diagnostics (Shapiro test is low-powered at n=12)")
```

# Post-hoc site-year comparisons

Use unadjusted Fisher's LSD-style pairwise tests **only when the corresponding site-year omnibus test is significant** (p < 0.05). These comparisons apply to site-years *within the same sampling event*. Do not compare pre-tillage against pre-rolling as though they were randomized treatments.

```{r posthoc}
pair_tables <- list()
for (event_name in event_levels) {
  if (models[[event_name]]$test$p_value < 0.05) {
    emm <- emmeans(models[[event_name]]$model, ~ site_year)
    tab <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(emm, adjust = "none"),
                                 infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))) |>
      mutate(event = event_name, .before = 1)
    pair_tables[[event_name]] <- tab
    cat("\n\n### ", event_name, "\n\n", sep = "")
    print(knitr::kable(tab, digits = 3,
                       caption = paste("Site-year comparisons:", event_name)))
  } else {
    cat("\n\n", event_name, ": omnibus site-year test not significant; no post-hoc tests.\n", sep = "")
  }
}
if (length(pair_tables)) {
  readr::write_csv(bind_rows(pair_tables),
                   file.path(out_dir, "site_year_fisher_lsd.csv"))
}
```

# Interpretation

Use the wide descriptive table in the site-year characteristics section. Report significant differences **within each sampling event** if supported by the model and residual checks. Site-year is an observational comparison combining field, year, rye variety, and management timing; the results are not causal estimates of any of those factors. Do not interpret the difference between early and late termination samples as a termination-method effect or a direct estimate of rye growth.
